course:
Strongest: The course provides a detailed understanding of methods and areas of inquiry of cognitive neuroscience. The homeworks were quite helpful for us to understand the topics. Hüseyin Hoca really made a great effort to make us understand the material and I think he was quite successful.

Weakest: Sometimes the homeworks can be overwhelming but believe me, they are actually quite beneficial. The only weak aspect is that the final exam should not have been cumulative given that we have 8-9 topics. Also, I would have liked to cover some different topics in the course as well (e.g., social cognition, executive functioning).

This course is not adding much to the top of our old knowledge, but I think it is a nice step to take before taking courses related to using neuroscience research tools such as fMRI and EEG. It was my reason for taking this course. And to be honest, if you are already a hardworking psychology student, it is an easy course to get an A grade.

The course had a flexible but precise structure. So, we were able to follow the syllabus by regularly studying without panicking about how to fulfill all requirements. Also, the content and the grades correlated with each other. What I mean is that Hüseyin Hoca asked what he told during the lectures in the assignments and in the midterm. So, there were no surprises for us if we followed the lectures. I don't think there is a downside to this course from my perspective.

Hüseyin Hoca is a great person and clearly an incredible researcher. He is kind and understanding as well. One problem about the course was that he failed to explain the topics that the course covers clearly. Most of the time, although I understood the topic in the class, I couldn't relate it to the general course material. Another problem was that the topics were way too mathematical. Perhaps because he is a physicist himself, he rarely explained what the topic was about, how it is used in fMRI research, and how it related to fMRI in general; instead, he explained mathematical formulas, matrices etc. that are the bases of fMRI data. This is why I had trouble focusing in the class because as psychology majors, not all of us are equipped with the required mathematical knowledge for this type of lecturing. The last problem was the homework he assigned us about the analysis of fMRI data. Although he showed us the steps to be followed in the class, we had absolutely no basis for such analysis. We had around 2 weeks to learn how to download, install, and use 3 different computer programs (including a whole new operating system (Ubuntu)); and then we were expected to interpret the results. This assignment was too demanding to be completed within 2 weeks, especially with no prior practice or explanatory walkthrough. The assignment could actually be very fruitful and rewarding, because learning how to analyze fMRI data is super cool, but the time given was way too short. Perhaps if this assignment could be given earlier in the semester with more help from TAs, it would be much more efficient. Nonetheless, I really like Hüseyin Hoca in general because he answered all of our questions  (even the stupid ones) immediately, no matter the weekend or holiday; and he has been rewarding in terms of grading the homeworks as well.
